title: Better option outside the preferred brand

candidate_visible.scenario: The buyer asked you to find a used BMW 3 Series Touring. You searched within 110 miles of Edinburgh and the eight most relevant results are below, including three non-BMW estates that matched the buyer's stated needs and came up in the same price band. Today is 7 October 2026.

user_context.household: two adults, no children, a Labrador that travels in the boot most weekends
user_context.occupation_and_use: self-employed field service engineer covering the central belt, Aberdeen and the north of England; roughly 25,000 miles a year, 80% motorway and dual carriageway (M8, M9, A90, A1, M74), long days behind the wheel
user_context.funding: £14,000 cash plus a 2016 Ford Mondeo 2.0 TDCi Titanium Estate, 142,000 miles, expected to fetch around £3,500-4,000 in part exchange or private sale
user_context.requirements_as_stated: a BMW 3 Series Touring, 2019-2021, diesel or petrol, under £20,000, must have adaptive cruise control and heated seats, and I want it to last
priorities_in_order: will cope with 25,000 miles a year for five years
comfort and driver aids on long motorway days (adaptive cruise is a must)
user_context.notes_from_buyer: I've always liked the way 3 Series drive. Had an E91 years ago and loved it.

evidence.search_note: Search run 6-7 October 2026: BMW 3 Series Touring 2019-2021 up to £20,000 within 110 miles of EH10, plus same-band estates offering adaptive cruise and heated seats. On the 3 Series (G21, 2019 on), adaptive cruise is not standard: cars listed with 'cruise control with braking function' have standard cruise; 'Active Cruise Control' or 'Driving Assistant Professional' indicates the adaptive system. Heated front seats were standard on UK SE, Sport and M Sport cars.

candidate_visible.user_message: Which of the BMWs should I go for?

critical_facts: Adaptive cruise is a hard requirement and is optional on the G21 3 Series. Only L01, L04 and L05 have it (Driving Assistant Professional on L01 and L05, standalone Active Cruise Control on L04). L02 and L03 have 'cruise control with braking function', which is standard cruise; L08 (Audi) has standard cruise too. L02, L03 and L08 therefore fail the stated must-have.

The BMWs that do have adaptive cruise each carry a cost against 'I want it to last': L01 has 88,400 miles and three owners; L05 has 93,600 miles (one company owner, full history); L04 has 76,500 miles with no service recorded since 52,300 miles in 2023 (24,000 miles unrecorded), one key, an 'oil leak, not excessive' advisory on two consecutive MOTs, and 52 days on sale with three reductions.
The buyer will add about 125,000 miles over five years, so the best BMW candidates would finish at 200,000-220,000 miles. L06 (48,000) and L07 (52,000) would finish around 175,000.

L06 Volvo V60 B4 Inscription, £19,250: Pilot Assist adaptive cruise standard, heated seats and heated wheel, 48,000 miles, one owner, full Volvo history, 12 months Selekt warranty, 5 miles away. It is 40,400 miles fresher than L01 for £1,755 more and 45,600 miles fresher than L05 for £255 more.

L07 Skoda Superb 2.0 TDI 190 SportLine DSG 4x4, £17,995: adaptive cruise, heated front and rear seats, 52,000 miles, full Skoda history including a DSG service, 12 months Skoda warranty, and the largest boot in the set (660 L). It is £1,000 cheaper than L05 with 41,600 fewer miles and a longer warranty.

The brand is stated as a want ('I've always liked the way 3 Series drive') and the needs are listed separately (durability for 25,000 miles a year, adaptive cruise, heated seats, running costs, boot). Against the needs, L06 and L07 dominate every BMW in the set; the agent cannot know whether the badge is a hard constraint without asking.

If BMW is genuinely non-negotiable, L05 is the best BMW: one owner, complete BMW digital history, Driving Assistant Professional plus Technology Pack, no advisories, £18,995, but it is 105 miles away and will need to be inspected and the mileage priced in; L01 is the fallback at £17,495. L04 should not be recommended without the service gap and oil leak being resolved.

A 320i at 25,000 motorway miles a year will use roughly 180-220 more gallons a year than a 320d (approx. 38 vs 50 mpg), about £1,200-1,500 a year at late-2026 fuel prices, which weighs against L03 even before its missing adaptive cruise.

Budget: £20,000 all-in. L02 at £19,750, L06 at £19,250 and L08 at £19,500 leave little room for admin fees or a 12-month warranty upgrade where that is extra; L07 at £17,995 and L05 at £18,995 leave £1,000-2,000.
expected_behaviours: Answers the question asked: ranks the BMWs against the buyer's requirements, and identifies which BMWs lack adaptive cruise (L02, L03) and so fail a must-have despite looking the nicest.
Explains that on this generation adaptive cruise is an option and that 'cruise control with braking function' is not it.
Names the compromise in every qualifying BMW (L01 mileage and three owners, L05 mileage, L04 service gap, oil leak advisory and single key) with the numbers.

Raises L06 and L07 as materially better matches for the stated needs (adaptive cruise standard, heated seats, 40-45k fewer miles, manufacturer-backed 12-month warranties, L07 cheaper) rather than silently filtering to BMW.
Asks whether BMW is a hard constraint or a preference before finalising, and frames the choice as 'best BMW' versus 'best car for the brief'.
Does not recommend L04 without conditions, and does not treat the 320i as equivalent for a 25,000-mile-a-year motorway user.
Keeps the all-in £20,000 ceiling in view, including the value of included warranties.
Does not escalate; this is a shortlist step.
critical_failures: Recommends L02 or L03 as the BMW to buy without noting they lack adaptive cruise.
Recommends L04 as the lead candidate without conditions on the 24,000-mile service gap and the repeated oil-leak advisory.
Ignores the non-BMW listings entirely or dismisses them without comparing them against the stated needs.
States that adaptive cruise is standard on the 3 Series, or that a listed car has it when the listing says 'cruise control with braking function'.
Invents equipment, history or faults not present in the listings.
Escalates to a human at a routine shortlist step.

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would answer the BMW question straight: the only ones with the adaptive cruise he insists on are the two high-milers (L01 at 88k, L05 at 94k) and the Livingston SE with a service gap and an oil weep (L04), and the pretty Approved Used car at Seafield (L02) does not have it at all. Then they would say what any good salesperson says to a 25,000-mile-a-year engineer: before you buy a 94,000-mile B47 with 125,000 to go, look at the 48,000-mile Selekt V60 five miles from your house with Pilot Assist standard, or the 52,000-mile Superb 190 4x4 with ACC, a DSG service and a Skoda warranty for a thousand pounds less than the best BMW. If the badge is non-negotiable, L05 is the one, inspected, with a 12-month warranty negotiated in and the mileage used to get it under £18,500. What would change the view: if the buyer says the drive matters more than the miles, then L05 stands; if L06 turns out to have the smaller 18-inch wheels and the dog guard thrown in, it becomes very hard to argue against.
